pr_title: do not evaluate constants in asm.js, fix IIFE mode detection
pr_body:
fixes #10283

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**
This PR basically disables the ConstPlugin in asm.js functions.

**Did you add tests for your changes?**
Yes, but it might not be the best place for it, please let me know if there is a better place.

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**
It should not cause any compatibility problems.

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**
Probably nothing.

If I open another PR to backport this to webpack 4, would you accept it?

There is something strange with this PR, it seems to fix the easy test cases, but on huge emscripten-generated asm.js files it somehow doesn't always recognize the asm.js parts. I'll try to reproduce the issue with a small test case.

The following is not recognized as asm.js:
```
(function() { "use asm"; return 0 == 0 ? 1 : 0; })();
```

This is true for "use strict" as well, it is not recognized properly in these cases, I'll try to understand why.

issue_context.title: ConstPlugin invalidates asm.js code
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the webpack Gitter. -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- https://gitter.im/webpack/webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**

ConstPlugin can change asm.js ("use asm") functions and invalidate them by inserting "false", "true", "undefined" values. In asm.js, using these identifiers are not allowed.

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

I'm currently trying to use https://www.npmjs.com/package/viz.js and compiling that with webpack causes it to no longer be valid asm.js code.
But this can be seen with much smaller codes as well, basically with any const conditional. (`0==0` becomes `true`, `truthy() ? 0 : 1` can become `truthy() ? 0 : undefined`, etc)

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**

I think the best would be to simply disable ConstPlugin inside asm.js functions as it would be much harder to properly inject valid asm.js code there. The Parser's scope could be extended to check for "use asm" expressions just like it checks "use strict", and then ConstPlugin could use that info to skip those parts.

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version: 4.41.5
